title: European Commission proposes associate membership for Canada
excerpt: The European Union and Canada are discussing a new partnership model that would align policies and governance without full accession.
bodyHtml:
The European Commission announced on October 29, 2026, that it is discussing the possibility of Canada becoming the first associate member of the European Union. President von der Leyen stated that the proposed model is an association without accession, intended to replace full membership with a common ambition and vision.

The proposal includes closer alignment on policies such as artificial intelligence, climate, energy, and security. It also entails increased cooperation between the European Commission and the Canadian government, as well as between their respective parliaments and courts. The European Union and Canada will also build a single space for strategic supply chains, which includes joint or complementary investment.

Additionally, the European Commission announced that Canada will join the European Union's infrastructure for supercomputing. This network includes twelve state-of-the-art supercomputers located across Europe. Furthermore, imports of Canadian critical raw materials to the European Union reached EUR 3.3 billion, that is CAD 5.18 billion, in the previous year.
topic: Keynote speech by President von der Leyen on EU-Canada relations at the C.D. Howe Institute
